where: the record strip and the identity block at the top of every record frame — the state family has no member for a person who was merged upstream mid-flight
finding: The brief's dangerous class has three members and the round renders two. `differs` and `orphaned` both have a phone strip; **merged upstream** — where `readThroughMerges` follows the trail and the edit lands on the survivor under a different id — has no presentation anywhere, and neither of the two that exist can say it without lying. sync-orphaned's strip says in words 'It has nowhere to land… Nothing is lost — the correction is still held here'; after a merge the correction *did* land, so that sentence is false. sync-differs' strip says 'At 9:08 the church office changed the same field to Ito' — a field-level story about one person, where the truth is that the person changed. Worse is the quiet case: if the survivor already holds what Marcus typed, no difference is detected, the job reports `landed`, and Tally's student now points at an upstream person nobody chose. On the phone that matters more than on the laptop, because the top 200 CSS px of every record frame — 'Ava Chen-Ito' at ~125–150, '10th grade' at ~164, the Allergies badge at ~180–200 — is three upstream-derived facts read at a glance, and the allergy line is the one field in this app where reading the wrong child's value is a physical risk. Marcus opens the record on Sunday, sees the surname he typed, and has nothing on the glass telling him the record under it is a different Planning Center person from the one he edited.
evidence: Zero occurrences of 'merge' in any of the sixteen prototype-sync files (the only hits are inside 'emergency'). The state marks now number eight — ▪ queued, → sending/stalled, ‖ waiting, ✓ landed, ≠ differs, ! failed/held, ⊘ orphaned, ◌ no record — and none of them means 'the person moved'. sync-orphaned--phone-fold: the ⊘ chip beside the name reads 'No Planning Center record', which asserts the exact opposite of a merge. sync-differs--phone-fold: the two-cell dl is 'ON THE RECORD NOW / Ito / the church office · 9:08' against 'YOU TYPED / Chen-Ito / you · 9:05' — a comparison of two values by two authors, with no slot for two ids. sync-profile--phone-fold: identity block device y250–405 (125–202 CSS px), all of it upstream-sourced.
direction: One more state on the strip that already exists, not a new object: keep the two-cell shape from `differs` but put people in it instead of values — the name the edit was sent to and the name it landed on, who merged them and when — with the one move being whether this Tally row follows the survivor. It has to fire on the id changing, not on the values differing, or the silent case never surfaces. Reuse the danger tone and one mark from the existing family; no new colour and no icon library, per the journey brief. If it is judged too expensive to draw, say so explicitly — but it should not go on being covered by two strips whose sentences are untrue of it.

where: 'Keep Ito' and 'Send Chen-Ito again', stacked full-width at roughly 529–572 and 581–625 CSS px down the record
finding: The round-2 finding is properly closed: neither move is the default now, both are matched ink-800 secondaries, the labels name the values so the choice is legible without re-reading the paragraph, the two cells sit on one baseline, and the live one is ringed. The choice is safe to make one-handed. What is left is geometry: the two buttons have opposite consequences — one leaves the church office's deliberate correction alone, one writes Chen-Ito back over it — and they are 44 CSS px tall with 8 CSS px between them, so the brief's own 8px mis-tap lands exactly in the gap and a 10px one lands on the other decision. Neither mis-tap is catastrophic (a wrong 'Send' re-queues into a state the queued strip says is still cancellable; a wrong 'Keep' costs a retype), which is why this is minor rather than major.
evidence: sync-differs--phone.html: both buttons `min-h-11 … w-full` = 44 CSS px, in a `flex flex-col gap-2` = 8 CSS px separation, identical `bg-ink-800 text-ink-100 ring-1 ring-ink-700` styling — so the only thing distinguishing the two targets under a thumb is the word. Measured on sync-differs--phone-fold: Keep Ito device y1058–1145, Send Chen-Ito again y1163–1250, 18 device px apart.
direction: Where two adjacent targets differ in consequence rather than in weight, the separation has to carry what the styling no longer can: a wider gap between these two specifically (gap-4 rather than gap-2), or 48px targets, which the brief calls comfortable and 44 marginal. Do not re-introduce a weight difference to separate them — that was the round-2 bug.
